description:
op-bcg and op-4ily were fixed on 2026-08-11 (commit 4feb6c84), but the agent doing that work was scoped to specific files and found three MORE instances it could not touch because another agent owned those files at the time.

STILL FALSE, verified present after the fix:
- crates/tampines/src/fluids/mod.rs:21 — cites "Marviken references" as a basis for the water EOS choice
- crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/drift_flux.rs:179 — "against Moody / Zaloudek / Marviken. Substituting an unvalidated..."
- crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/drift_flux.rs:1052 — "Moody / Zaloudek / Marviken — rather than introducing a second choking..."

THE FACTS, verified in the working tree: marviken_tests.rs:116 is #[ignore = "skip first, Marviken is more complex"], its sole assertion is COMMENTED OUT at line 218, and the body ends in todo!() at line 222. Marviken is digitised but never gated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY VALIDATED, so the correction does not overshoot: Moody has 13 active isobar tests with MOODY_LOG10_TOL = 0.06 and MOODY_DEEP_LOG10_TOL = 0.08 absolute on |log10 G|, with validate_moody_isobar_inner explicitly skipping points that are neither Region 4 nor deep-subcooled. Zaloudek has 21/22/21/4/21 tests across five files, pressure tolerance 0.005-0.05, mass-flux log10 tolerance 0.05 — but these are GRAPH-READ HEM curves, not experimental data, which is its own caveat. Edwards-O Brien IS genuinely validated and its two tests pass.

Fix by correcting the claim, NOT by performing the validation. Under VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md a false validation claim is worse than none, because it survives review by looking right. Follow the pattern already applied in crates/tampines/src/critical_flow/mod.rs, which now carries a three-bullet V&V status block naming what is gated, with what tolerances, and what is not.
title: tampines: three more false Marviken validation claims outside the op-bcg fix scope

description: Snap the carved staircase boundary points onto the surface: for each point used by a boundary/walls face, move it to its closest point on the triangle-soup surface (closest-point-on-triangle, Ericson). description:
Discrete coolant channel model, block-level conduction, gap radiation for the prismatic HTTR core.

THE PRISMATIC GOTCHA, per the maintainer: BLOCK BYPASS FLOW. A meaningful fraction of total flow, load-dependent, and routinely the largest single source of code-to-experiment disagreement. Implement it EXPLICITLY, not as a lumped fudge factor.

Note the workspace history: htgr_sim_v1 was originally prismatic and is being retargeted to HTR-10 pebble bed under op-jyyp. This bead is the prismatic core coming BACK as a first-class geometry alongside the pebble bed, behind the Phase 2.1 closure trait - not a revert of op-jyyp.

Gated on Phase 2.1 and on the TAMPINES sequencing gate.
title: HTGR Phase 2.3: prismatic (HTTR) core thermal-hydraulics incl. block bypass flow

description:
The graphite/moderator reactivity channel itself has landed as `crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/feedback.rs` (GraphiteModeratorFeedback: own temperature state, own caller-supplied coefficient, lumped m*cp ODE step, thermal time constant; 6 tests green). What remains of op-jyyp.6 is the KINETICS WIRING, which deliberately did NOT go in the tampines library:

- The tampines library is free of teh-o-prke (it is only an Android-gated dev-dependency), so feedback.rs returns a plain dimensionless reactivity for a caller to sum with a fuel Doppler term and feed to a kinetics solver.
- The wiring therefore belongs in an example or in nee_soon, where a neutronics dependency is appropriate. Do not add teh-o-prke to the tampines library to close this.

Also outstanding, and the real blocker on any quantitative use: a MODERATOR-ONLY temperature coefficient. None is supplied, on purpose. The published HTR-10 figures in IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2 Table 4-33 (NRG -7.37e-5/-8.05e-5 per C; INET/VSOP -7.49e-5/-9.15e-5 per C) are ISOTHERMAL coefficients (fuel + moderator moved together); they are exposed in feedback.rs as clearly-labelled constants for validating a whole-core isothermal calculation, and using one as alpha_m would double-count fuel Doppler. A moderator-only coefficient has to come from a neutronics calculation that perturbs the moderator alone (rung 3 -> rung 4 hand-off, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 5.4).

Measured supporting figure (2026-08-11, feedback.rs::graphite_thermal_time_constant_is_long): the derived HTR-10 pebble-graphite inventory of 5129.16 kg against a bed conductance of 97473.9 W/K gives a thermal time constant of 89.37 s - and that is the pebbles alone, excluding the 1 m side reflector. Against an effectively instantaneous fuel Doppler response, this is why the two channels must stay separate.
title: HTR-10: wire the graphite/moderator feedback channel into PRKE (remainder of op-jyyp.6)

description: op-9vml shipped the cross-reference-jump half (list a project's documents, jump to PDF/markdown). This closes the other half explicitly requested: an in-GUI editor for the project's one .bib file -- list entries (via kovan_literature::parse_bib_entries, op-vi1n), add a new entry, edit an existing entry's fields, delete an entry, write the file back out. Needs a bib-entry-to-text serializer (kovan_literature::to_bibtex only takes a full KovanDocument, not a raw BibEntry -- either build a lightweight BibEntry serializer or thread through minimal KovanDocument fields).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented. Two pieces:

1. crates/kovan-literature/src/bibtex.rs: `render_entry`/`render_entries` -- the write side alongside op-vi1n's `parse_bib_entries`, taking a raw `BibEntry` (not a full `KovanDocument`, which `to_bibtex` needs) and producing BibTeX text. Deliberately not a byte-for-byte round trip (field order becomes the BTreeMap's alphabetical order; comments/whitespace outside entries are not preserved) -- documented as such, consistent with op-vi1n's own "deliberately one-way and shallow" scoping. 2 new tests (round-trips through parse_bib_entries; joins multiple entries).

2. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/bibliography.rs: a JabRef-like entry editor added alongside the existing cross-reference browser. `EntryEditor` holds an in-progress add/edit as an ordered `Vec<(name, value)>` (not a BTreeMap directly, so the UI can show a stable field order and support adding a blank field row). List/Edit/Delete/+New entry/+field, cite-key-required validation. Saving fully rewrites the project's `.bib` file from the in-memory entry list via `render_entries`, then re-opens the project so `kovan.toml`'s cite-key join immediately reflects any cite-key change.

cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android, after fixing 2 borrow-checker conflicts from calling &mut self methods from inside a closure that also borrowed self.entries). cargo test --release: 187 kovan + 54 kovan-literature lib tests passing. Not committed yet.

This closes op-9vml's remaining half -- both the cross-reference browser and the .bib editor are now implemented.

title: kovan-gui: JabRef-like .bib entry editor (add/edit/delete, write back to file) -- op-9vml's remaining half
